narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 58% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That is only modestly above the cutoff, but it was enough for the bank to decline.

Among all factors, the amount you requested was by far the strongest reason for the denial. You asked for 13,756 DM, while approved applicants typically request about 3,020 DM. A loan that large relative to the dataset makes repayment look riskier, so it pushed most strongly toward bad credit.

Your checking-account status was the next most influential factor, and it worked in your favor. Having no checking account is not unusual: about 59% of approved applicants also had this status, so it did not count against you.

Your savings status was the third most influential factor, also working in your favor. With unknown or no savings, you are in the same group as roughly 33% of approved applicants, so this feature supported your case rather than hurting it.

Even so, the requested amount was powerful enough to outweigh those favorable signals and raise the predicted risk above the denial threshold.

Next, consider applying for a smaller amount closer to typical approved requests, or shortening the term. Providing evidence of savings, a guarantor, or other security could also strengthen a future application. Ask the bank what specific amount or terms would improve your chances.

 Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
